study.question: Can exact stable prefix-rank compaction replace the second per-history sort in the already shared temporal executor, reducing computation while preserving precisely the selected information and parameterized prediction function?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: history_g1_r0026_shared_temporal.py invokes unchanged _transition_support once, but that support still performs a chronological sort followed by argsort of unique compaction keys. A prefix count for singleton and excluded positions yields a bijective scatter into identical stable compact order. Removing the second sort may lower measured execution cost without altering eligibility, ties, adjacency, counts, model capacity or information. CUDA scan/scatter overhead could erase or reverse this benefit; this is an execution hypothesis, not a new predictive-information hypothesis.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit shared sufficient-count execution completely; replace only its second sorting operation by prefix ranks and collision-free permutation scatter. No readout or fitted representation changes.

DIN discusses grouped pooling, target-dependent weighted aggregation, intensity and noisy behavioral sequences. The local baseline is a field-adapted softmax reference, not exact DIN. This follow-up preserves existing field/match-group readouts and temporal count information; it neither adopts a new attention unit nor attributes an execution effect to DIN.

Author README warns histories contain category/brand/type and no item. Those information limits remain fixed. Publisher full paper remains unavailable; no detailed DMR reproduction or mechanism comparison is asserted.

inherited_components: All 10 class ASTs from the shared temporal module are retained exactly, except final Model renamed _SortedSharedModel.
Underlying incumbent g1-r0024-run_zero architecture and parameters, including dormant allocations.
Existing one-chronology selected transition/gap/timing/symmetric-serial readouts and left-to-right residual addition order.
Original chronological age sort, complete-pair filtering, exclusion of every tied timestamp and causal support definition.
Inherited 35 label-free first512 diagnostic scalars, scalar temporal oracle on first8 rows and same-checkpoint legacy/shared comparisons.
study.proposed_difference: Append a parameter-free Model subclass. For singleton flags s in chronological sorted order, destination is cumsum(s)-1 for accepted events and n+cumsum(~s)-1 for excluded events. These are disjoint contiguous ranges covering every position exactly once. Scatter the sorted positions to destination and gather original event indices. This produces the same stable order as argsort(where(s,position,position+L)), including invalid suffix. No inputs, learnable components, caches, persistent batch state, RNG draws, optimizer/loss or frozen contracts change. CONFIG support_execution=scatter; sort delegates to the unchanged ancestor method for diagnostics/control compatibility. Generic scan/scatter compaction has no algorithmic-priority claim; authorized paper and agent searches for stream compaction returned no additional sources, so a nearest-algorithm literature review remains incomplete.
predictions: Exact integer support agreement on observed rows and empty, length0/1/2, all-tied, missing-field and reversed-input probes; all inherited raw count differences and scalar oracle errors remain zero (fractional product oracle tolerance2e-5 as inherited).

Inherited transformed-feature/logit comparisons remain within1e-6 on first512 rows. Source preservation plus exact support equality implies identical real-arithmetic hypothesis class and parameter gradients; this is not a measured CUDA gradient equality claim.
Expected allocated parameters17254067 = embedding17078688 + dense175379, with zero new parameters and no RNG change. Host count is authoritative.

If second-sort overhead matters at B4096,L128, whole-batch p50/p95, train seconds and wall time decrease relative to g1-r0026-shared_temporal (777.895747s wall,667.398759s train; p50 29.793665ms,p95 31.087571ms; throughput129877.668/s; peak722083328 bytes). Efficiency is not established by source operation counts.

No directional AUC improvement predicted. Compare full-population AUC/logloss and supplied slices at matching recipe/data passes; any score difference is descriptive until paired repetitions discriminate numerical training drift.
falsifiers: Any supported event/order/count mismatch falsifies exact compaction and blocks interpreting cost as the same-function contrast. Invalid-tail mismatch alone should be examined separately because suffix events carry zero mass.
Any nonfinite output, excessive diagnostic error, changed parameter count or unintended source modification invalidates the execution-equivalence claim.
Wall/train and batch latency that do not improve falsify the proposed practical cost benefit at this batch/history size, even with perfect index equality.
An adverse quality/cost observation prevents selecting the candidate as an empirical efficiency improvement; single-seed score variation cannot establish preserved generalization.
alternative_explanations: GPU prefix scans, scatter traffic, synchronization and launch overhead may cost more than sorting128 elements.
Kernel scheduling, device clocks, host gathering and resource contention can explain small timing changes. Historical cost comparisons lack simultaneous hardware controls.
Different integer-support implementation can alter launch scheduling and floating-point downstream reduction behavior; prior shared versus legacy AUC differed despite matched diagnostic features.
First512 diagnostic rows and scalar/unit checks cannot establish tensor correctness on every population history or gradient equivalence.
Static publisher snapshots have undocumented as-of dates; this benchmark does not establish production point-in-time validity.
